title: Bonk's Revenge
subtitle: Another headlong prehistoric journey
summary: Bonk's Revenge is the second PC Engine adventure of Hudson's caveman hero, first released in Japan on 19 July 1991.
body: Bonk's Revenge is the second PC Engine adventure of Hudson's caveman hero, first released in Japan on 19 July 1991. King Drool III has stolen half the Moon, sending Bonk through another cartoon world to recover it. The stages range from outdoor landscapes to trains, water and space. Bonk's head remains his principal weapon, and the sequel builds around the pleasure of turning a simple jump into a forceful landing while the setting supplies another unusual surface or creature to cross.

Holding the attack button in midair lets Bonk spin and hover, stretching the distance and control of a jump. His mouth can grip certain surfaces for climbing, opening another route through the scenery. Hearts represent health, fruit restores it, and blue hearts can extend the available supply. Smileys collected along the way contribute to bonus opportunities after a boss. These systems make the path through a stage more than a dash to its exit, rewarding careful movement and attention to items placed above or beyond the most obvious route.

Meat powers Bonk into stronger temporary forms. At an intermediate stage, his attacks can freeze enemies; at full power, fire and invulnerability turn movement through a crowded screen into a brief advantage. The player can use that window to press forward or tackle a difficult section. Red Company and Mutech developed the game, with music by Hirohiko Takayama. Its expanded movement and expressive transformations continue the first game's central idea: a character's comically oversized body can supply an entire platform game's vocabulary.
